claim: Fix integers \(n\ge2\) and \(1\le c<n\). Consider connected binary bipartite incidence matrices with two row species, \(n\) column species, no isolated species, and exactly \(E=n+c\) interactions. Let \(\mathcal N\) denote the conventional degree-ordered NODF index normalized to the interval \([0,1]\) using all \(K=1+\binom n2\) row/column unordered pairs, and let \(Q^\star\) be Barber bipartite modularity maximized over every partition of all \(n+2\) species. Exactly \(c\) columns have degree two and \(s=n-c\) have degree one. If \(x\) is the larger count of degree-one columns exclusive to one row, then \(\lceil s/2\rceil\le x\le s\), and each such integer determines exactly one incidence-matrix isomorphism class. The entire attainable ordered metric locus is \(\mathcal N_x=[cs+\mathbf 1_{\{2x>s\}}c/(n-x)]/[1+\binom n2]\) and \(Q_x^\star=2x(n-x)/(n+c)^2\). The complete Pareto frontier for jointly maximizing the two metrics comprises exactly the classes \(x\in\{x_0,\ldots,s\}\) where \(x_0=\min(s,\lceil n/2\rceil)\). The unique NODF-maximizing class is the Ferrers matrix \(x=s\); it simultaneously attains maximum Barber modularity if and only if \(c\ge s-1\), equivalently \(2c\ge n-1\). When \(2c<n-1\), the frontier contains more than one non-dominated class, so there is a strict nestedness–modularity tradeoff. For example, when \(n=6,c=1\), the frontier consists of \(x=3,4,5\) with respective \((\mathcal N,Q^\star)\) scores \((1/3,18/49)\), \((11/32,16/49)\), and \((3/8,10/49)\). The theorem holds for arbitrary \(n,c\) in the stated range; exact enumeration is used only to verify small instances.
integrity: Formulas proved for arbitrary dimensions using exhaustive column types, global community-partition reduction, and exact quadratic Pareto comparison. Independent small-case direct NODF, exhaustive vertex-partition modularity, and integer Pareto computations use exact rational arithmetic; finite tests do not replace the universal proof.
scientific_limitations: Binary, connected, two-row incidence matrices with no isolated species and exactly n+c links, 1<=c<n; normalized classical NODF and globally optimized Barber bipartite modularity. Does not extend automatically to larger guilds, weighted edges, other nestedness/modularity versions, or null-model corrected scores.
title: Exact nestedness–modularity Pareto frontier in connected two-by-\(n\) ecological networks
